title: exit-plan
description: Structured second-line exit plan record for a third-party arrangement at a regulated financial institution. Carries the trigger set, transition target options and the chosen target, time-to-transition against the firm's impact tolerance, the data-extraction-return-and-destruction set, the contract-termination mechanics, the customer- and regulator-notice posture, the supervisory-readiness posture during transition, the test history, and the named approver. Consumes the vendor-diligence record (criticality, subcontractors, data_access, residual_risk, exit_plan_status). Downstream consumers: dora-register-builder for ICT-third-party register entries where DORA applies; resilience-testing-pack for exit-rehearsal scenarios; concentration-risk-review for the substitutability read.

arrangement_id.description: Stable identifier for the vendor arrangement. Reused across criticality-assessment, vendor-diligence, contract-gap-review, concentration-risk-review.

vendor_diligence_record_id.description: Pointer to the vendor-diligence record this plan was built against. The plan consumes criticality, subcontractors, data_access, residual_risk, exit_plan_status from that record.

engagement_id.description: Optional pointer to the engagement-scope record under which this plan was produced.

as_of_date.description: Date the plan was last revised.

review_type.description: Why this plan is being produced or revised. Drives depth and review-gate set.

vendor_legal_name.description: Counterparty legal entity name. Use the contracting entity, not the brand.

service_type.description: Concise service description, e.g., core banking SaaS, transfer agent, claims TPA, foundation-model API, BIN-sponsor processor.

business_process_supported.description: Name of the firm's business process the vendor supports.

important_business_service.description: If the firm has an IBS map, the IBS the vendor sits in. Drives the impact-tolerance test.

criticality.description: Sourced from criticality-assessment via vendor-diligence. The plan consumes; it does not set.

dora_in_scope.description: True when the arrangement supports a critical or important function under DORA Article 28(8). Triggers the DORA exit-strategy expectation set.

data_access.description: Categories of firm or customer data the vendor holds at termination. Drives the data-return-and-destruction obligation set. Sourced from vendor-diligence.

subcontractors.description: Material fourth parties in the chain. Drives fourth-party-bottleneck analysis on transition.

residual_risk_input.description: Residual risk read from the vendor-diligence record at the time of plan drafting.

ai_vendor.description: True when the vendor supplies an AI system. Triggers AI-specific transition considerations: prompt-template portability, RAG-corpus migration, model-version pinning, deprecation-notice handling.

triggers.description: Events that would activate this plan. Cover vendor-driven, firm-driven, regulator-driven, and market-driven categories. A plan covering only one category is incomplete.

lead_time_assumption.description: Realistic lead time the firm would have under this trigger. Distress and unexpected termination usually have shorter lead times than annual recertification.

detection_signal.description: How the firm would learn the trigger fired. Press, regulator notice, vendor notice, monitoring KRI breach, fourth-party event.

transition_target_options.description: The realistic alternatives the firm has assessed. Each option is scored on viability and time-to-transition. A plan with one option only is a single point of failure.

candidate_named.description: Specific substitute candidate or in-source target where identified. May be 'unidentified' for an unsourced substitute.

time_to_transition.description: Realistic elapsed time. State the assumption set.

dependencies.description: Capabilities, contracts, hires, builds, or fourth-party arrangements required to make this option real.

selected_transition_target.description: The firm's primary planned transition target. Names the option from transition_target_options designated 'primary'.

secondary_transition_target.description: Backup option for cases where the primary is unavailable (regulator forces a faster cutover, candidate substitute fails its own diligence, fourth-party bottleneck blocks the primary path).

time_to_transition_vs_tolerance.description: Whether the planned time-to-transition fits the firm's impact tolerance for the supported important business service. 'breach' is itself a finding, not a plan.

data_return_and_destruction.description: The data-return, data-migration, and data-destruction set. Build for every data category in data_access.

extraction_format.description: Format the vendor will return data in. Specify file format, schema, and whether vendor-proprietary or open.

schema_mapping_required.description: True when the substitute or in-source target uses a different schema. Drives migration-engineering effort.

extraction_window.description: Realistic time the extraction itself takes once initiated.

validation_against_firm_of_record.description: How the firm will validate the returned data against its own books-and-records or system-of-record.

vendor_obligations.description: What the contract obligates the vendor to do (formats, windows, transition assistance, key-material return). Pointer to contract-gap-review for the clause-by-clause read.

firm_obligations.description: What the firm must do (provision target, supply credentials, accept handover, schedule cutover, run UAT).

destruction_evidence_required.description: Form of vendor attestation of destruction (signed certificate, log evidence, third-party audit). Specify retention of the destruction evidence at the firm.

post_termination_retention.description: Lawful retention by the vendor after termination (regulatory archive, fraud investigation, legal hold). Must be carved out of the destruction obligation explicitly.

key_rotation_and_revocation.description: Cyber-side cutover: revoke vendor access, rotate shared keys and tokens, decommission tunnels, remove DNS, update DLP rules.

documentation_set.description: What documentation the vendor must hand over: runbooks, configuration baselines, integration specs, model cards and prompt templates for AI vendors.

personnel_transition.description: Vendor-personnel posture during transition: named SMEs, knowledge-transfer sessions, reverse-shadowing for in-source paths.

code_and_artifact_escrow.description: Source code, build artifacts, container images, model weights, prompt libraries, RAG corpora held in escrow or returned at termination.

contract_termination_mechanics.description: Reads the operative termination terms. Pointer to contract-gap-review for the gap analysis.

termination_clause_reference.description: Section reference in the executed agreement. Note jurisdictional governing law.

termination_for_convenience.description: True when the firm has a unilateral termination-for-convenience right.

termination_assistance_period.description: Vendor's contractual transition-assistance commitment. The clause is not the plan.

termination_fees.description: Fee posture on early or for-convenience termination.

regulator_directed_termination_clause.description: True when the contract explicitly preserves the firm's ability to terminate on regulator direction without penalty. Banking and EBA-outsourcing-aligned contracts expect this.

in_flight_data_lock_in.description: Where the contract or product creates lock-in independent of the termination clause: vendor-proprietary data formats, model-fine-tune artifacts, custodial assets requiring third-party movement, regulator-licensed registrations.

customer_notice_posture.description: Customer-facing notification on planned and unexpected termination. Sector-specific obligations (Reg E, Reg DD, NACHA, fund prospectus updates, policyholder notices) live in the sector overlays.

lead_time.description: Required lead time. Reg E §1005.8 change-in-terms is one common anchor; sector overlays carry the rest.

channel.description: Statement, email, in-app notice, mailed letter, advance change-in-terms notice.

regulated_clock.description: Named regulator clock that drives the lead time, where one applies.

regulator_notice_posture.description: Supervisory notification on activation, in-flight, and post-cutover. A critical or important function exit usually lands on a supervisory notification clock; missing this is itself a finding.

notifiable_regimes.description: Named regimes (DORA Article 28 ICT-third-party register update; bank-regulator material-vendor change notification; Form ADV brochure update; Form N-CEN service-provider change; NAIC ORSA update; NYDFS event-reporting).

filings_triggered.description: Specific filings or registrations that have to update on transition.

supervisory_engagement_posture.description: How the firm will keep its supervisor informed during transition. For a critical or important function transition, expect proactive supervisory engagement, not only on-paper notice.

cyber_considerations.description: Cyber overlay during transition: secure data extraction; key rotation; access revocation choreography; vendor-side destruction certification; SEC cyber-disclosure exposure on a forced or contested termination; SIEM and DLP rule updates. Detail in references/cross-cutting/cyber.md.

privacy_considerations.description: Privacy overlay during transition: GLBA Safeguards data-handling on transition; state-privacy-law deletion and return obligations; HIPAA business-associate transition where in scope; cross-border data flows during transition. Detail in references/cross-cutting/privacy.md.

supervisory_readiness_during_transition.description: How the firm sustains supervisory and audit readiness during a multi-month transition: dual-running controls, evidence-collection across both vendors, MRA / MRIA exposure, examination-access continuity under the Bank Service Company Act for banks, books-and-records continuity for advisers and BDs.

fourth_party_dependencies.description: Subcontractors of the exiting vendor whose own posture creates a transition bottleneck (hyperscaler region, BIN-sponsor processor, KYC vendor, fund-accountant subcontractor, foundation-model upstream).

ai_specific_transition_considerations.description: Populated only when ai_vendor is true. AI-specific transition engineering does not collapse into generic data-extraction language.

prompt_template_portability.description: Whether the firm's prompt templates carry across to the substitute model vendor. Templates are usually model-specific.

rag_corpus_migration.description: Whether the embedded knowledge base, retrieval pipelines, and vector indices are vendor-portable or require re-embedding and re-indexing.

fine_tune_artifact_handling.description: Whether vendor-side fine-tune artifacts are returned, destroyed, or stranded.

model_version_pin_handling.description: The deployed checkpoint at termination; whether the vendor provides a final-version export or whether deprecation forces an earlier transition.

guardrail_and_eval_porting.description: Carrier-side guardrails and evaluation harnesses configured against the outgoing model usually need rework on the new model.

agent_tool_offboarding.description: For agentic vendors, the action-authorisation surface, tool whitelists, and audit-trail sinks must be revoked and rewired to the substitute or to the in-source agent.

cost_estimate_range.description: Order-of-magnitude transition cost band. Specify the cost-driver assumptions, not a false-precision number.

testing_plan.description: Test cadence, methods, and history. A plan never tested has unknown viability.

cadence.description: Tabletop / walkthrough / partial-simulation / full-live cadence per criticality tier and the firm's policy.

last_test_outcome.description: Pass / pass-with-findings / fail; summarise findings. 'Never tested' is honest and gets surfaced.

resilience_testing_pack_record_id.description: Pointer to the resilience-testing-pack record where the exit rehearsal sits in the integrated test programme.

exit_plan_status.description: Status flowing back to vendor-diligence and to dora-register-builder. 'Missing' on a critical or important arrangement is itself a finding.

open_dependencies_and_risks.description: Dependencies and risks that have to close before the plan is anything more than paper.

reviewer_questions.description: Questions for the human approver. Each names the decision it supports.

review_gates.description: Named human-review gates this plan must clear. Drawn from references/review-gates.md.

owner.description: Role accountable for keeping the plan current and tested. Usually the IBS owner or the head of TPRM. Procurement supports execution but does not own customer-facing impact.

approver.description: Role of the human approver named in the firm's third-party-risk and operational-resilience policy for this criticality tier.

next_review_trigger.description: Annual cycle date, scope-change trigger, contract-amendment trigger, vendor-incident-driven re-review condition.

confidence_label.description: Confidence in the overall plan, per references/review-gates.md.

source_trace.description: Citations supporting material claims. Every claim should be traceable.
